hc_curator.text: Calanais I is the best known, but there are other circles within sight, Calanais II and III and more. The whole landscape was set out as a sacred place.
The stones are standing on peat now, but about 1857 the local landowner ordered the peat cleared away from around them, and found the base of the stones and the chambered cairn inside the ring.
On the midsummer full moon, in the lunar standstill years, the moon rolls low along the hills and seems to set into the stones. Come back in 2025 or 2043 to see it. We'll leave the lights on.
The stones are glas, grey: Lewisian gneiss, some of the oldest rock in Europe. The peat round them is donn, brown, and a good deal younger.

hc_walker.text: I walked round it three times. Once for each time somebody told me not to touch the stones. They're so warm! Unless it's raining. Then they're just wet.
